The [[Olivetti]] '''Summa Prima 20''' is a [[Mechanical calculator|mechanical]], hand-operated add-listing machine produced between 1960 and 1974.<ref name="jaap-prima20-years">{{cite web
 |title=Olivetti (models table: Summa Prima 20 10×11, 1960–1974)
 |url=https://www.jaapsch.net/mechcalc/olivetti.htm
 |website=Jaap's Mechanical Calculators Page
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref> It prints entries and results onto a small [[Till roll|paper roll]], using an [[ink ribbon]], giving a permanent record of calculations.<ref name="computinghistory-paperroll">{{cite web
 |title=Olivetti Summa Prima 20 - Calculator
 |url=https://www.computinghistory.org.uk/det/6012/Olivetti-Summa-Prima-20/
 |website=The Centre for Computing History
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref> Each time the operating handle is pulled, the entered number is printed and added to an internal running total – "[[Computer memory|memory]]" – which made the machine useful for everyday [[accounting]] and cashier-style work.<ref name="bht-howtouse">{{cite web
 |title=OLIVETTI SUMMA PRIMA 20 (How to use: addition, subtraction, non-add, subtotal, total)
 |url=https://public.bht-berlin.de/hamann/olivetti/o-add/index2.html
 |website=public.bht-berlin.de (Christian Hamann)
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref>

== Interface ==
The machine is operated by pulling the main handle, which drives the internal mechanism and performs the selected function in a single cycle.<ref name="bht-howtouse"/> The Summa Prima 20 is designed for one-handed use, with the function control placed so it can be flicked by the right thumb just before pulling the handle.<ref name="johnwolff-joystick">{{cite web
 |title=Olivetti Mechanical Calculators (Prima 20 overview and function joystick)
 |url=https://www.johnwolff.id.au/calculators/Olivetti/Olivetti.htm
 |website=John Wolff's Web Museum
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref>

Numbers are entered on a 10-key [[keypad]]. A small window beside the keyboard shows the number of digits entered, and if a wrong digit is entered the keyboard can be cleared using the black spherical clearing lever.<ref name="bht-howtouse"/>

For repeated entry of the same number (commonly used for multiplication by repeated addition), the '''Repeat''' switch (marked '''X''') is set before the cycle. With Repeat enabled, the keyboard is not cleared after the handle is released, so the same value can be entered again on the next pull.<ref name="bht-howtouse"/>

Changing the operation type is done with the four-way function control, often described as a function “[[joystick]]”. The directions correspond to the printed symbols:
* '''Add''' (default): the control returns to the centre position for normal addition cycles.<ref name="bht-howtouse"/>
* '''Subtract''' ('''-''', right): set the control to '''-''' before pulling the handle. A separate right-hand lever can be used to lock the subtraction setting for multiple negative entries.<ref name="bht-howtouse"/>
* '''Total''' ('''*''', up): prints the total (in red) and clears the running total (“memory”) after the cycle.<ref name="bht-howtouse"/>
* '''Subtotal''' ('''◊''', down): prints the current accumulated sum (in red) while keeping the running total in memory.<ref name="bht-howtouse"/>
* '''Non-add''' ('''<''', left): prints the entered number without adding or subtracting it from the running total (useful for item numbers or reference entries).<ref name="bht-howtouse"/>

=== Paper handling and printing ===
The machine advances the [[printout]] automatically with each cycle. It also has a manual paper-feed knob, used to advance the paper without performing a calculation cycle.<ref name="bht-prima20-ops">{{cite web
 |title=OLIVETTI SUMMA PRIMA 20 (technical data and operating notes)
 |url=https://public.bht-berlin.de/hamann/olivetti/o-add/index2.html
 |website=public.bht-berlin.de (Christian Hamann)
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref> The paper roll is held in a fork at the back of the machine; the left, movable holder can be shifted to the left so the roll can be lifted out.<ref name="prima20-manual-paperroll">{{cite web
 |title=Gebrauchsanweisung für die schreibende Addiermaschine Olivetti Summa Prima 20 (PDF)
 |url=https://www.jaapsch.net/mechcalc/pdf/summaprima20manual.pdf
 |website=Jaap's Mechanical Calculators Page
 |publisher=Ing. C. Olivetti &amp; C., S.p.A.
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref> To remove the paper from the feed path, the left holder is pulled up, and the paper strip is pulled out.<ref name="bht-prima20-ops"/>

== Model differences ==
There were several versions of the Olivetti '''Summa Prima 20''', mainly depending on the currency system used in the target country, and on later production changes (keys and casing).<ref name="rechnerlexikon-variants">{{cite web
 |title=Olivetti Summa Prima 20 (variants: English versions, WN key, post-1972 square keys, Restysuma 20 name)
 |url=https://rechnerlexikon.de/artikel/Olivetti_Summa_Prima_20
 |website=Rechnerlexikon.de
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref><ref name="johnwolff-latemodel">{{cite web
 |title=Olivetti Mechanical Calculators (Prima 20: late model with square keytops and plastic base tray)
 |url=https://www.johnwolff.id.au/calculators/Olivetti/Olivetti.htm
 |website=John Wolff's Web Museum
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref>

=== Currency / keyboard variants (decimal vs £sd) ===
Some Prima 20 machines were built for standard decimal entry, while others were made for the pre-decimal British '''£/s/d''' (pounds, shillings, pence) system and have extra keys to handle that format.<ref name="cch-predecimal">{{cite web
 |title=Olivetti Summa Prima 20 (pre-decimal) - Calculator
 |url=https://www.computinghistory.org.uk/det/43093/Olivetti-Summa-Prima-20-%28pre-decimal%29/
 |website=The Centre for Computing History
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref><ref name="rechnerlexikon-variants"/>

* '''£sd (“Sterling”) versions''': these are documented with extra keys (commonly '''10''' and '''11''') above the normal 10-key keypad, used for pounds/shillings/pence working.<ref name="rechnerlexikon-variants"/><ref name="vintagecalcs-sterling-mult">{{cite web
 |title=Sterling Currency (£sd) Multiplication on a 12-key Add-Lister (Prima 20 with 10/12 and 11/12 keys)
 |url=https://www.vintagecalculators.com/html/sterling_currency_multiplication.html
 |website=VintageCalculators.com
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref>
* '''Switchable decimal ↔ £sd versions''': one documented English version uses a small lever on the underside of the machine to switch between decimal and English computations.<ref name="rechnerlexikon-variants"/><ref name="bobmockford-switch">{{cite web
 |title=Calculating Museum (Olivetti 20 £sd: switching via lever on underside)
 |url=https://www.bob-mockford.co.uk/museum/calculating/
 |website=Bob Mockford Online
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref>
* '''Alternative English switching (WN key)''': another English version is documented where switching is done via an additional '''WN''' ('''Whole Numbers''') key instead of an underside lever.<ref name="rechnerlexikon-variants"/>

Because the £sd machines add extra keys and special handling for old currency, they can look like they support “fraction-style” entry compared with the plain decimal model (for example, the extra 10/12 and 11/12 keys used for 10 pence and 11 pence in £sd calculations).<ref name="vintagecalcs-sterling-mult"/>

=== Named / catalogued variants (collector lists) ===
Collector catalogues also list named Prima 20 variants, including:
* '''Summa Prima 20 Simplex'''
* '''Summa Prima 20 Sterlina Mod 71'''
* '''Summa Prima 20 Sterlina Mod 71 Simplex'''<ref name="bardel-list">{{cite web
 |title=Michel Bardel's list (includes: Summa Prima 20 Simplex; Summa Prima 20 Sterlina Mod 71; Mod 71 Simplex)
 |url=https://www.rechenwerkzeug.de/Bardel/machn_q.htm
 |website=Rechenwerkzeug.de
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref>

=== Production changes (early vs late machines) ===
Documented Prima 20 examples show visible differences between earlier and later production:
* '''Keytops''': later machines are documented with '''square keytops'''.<ref name="rechnerlexikon-variants"/><ref name="johnwolff-latemodel"/>
* '''Casing / base''': John Wolff documents a late-model Prima 20 where the sheet-metal base was replaced by a '''plastic tray''', and the joystick area is surrounded by a '''white plastic bezel'''.<ref name="johnwolff-latemodel"/>

(These changes are consistent with weight/cost-saving design updates, especially as electronic calculators became common in the early 1970s and replaced many add-listing machines in everyday office use.)<ref name="johnwolff-electronic">{{cite web
 |title=Olivetti Mechanical Calculators (Prima 20 retired in early 1970s in favour of electronic calculators)
 |url=https://www.johnwolff.id.au/calculators/Olivetti/Olivetti.htm
 |website=John Wolff's Web Museum
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref>

=== Regional production / rebrands ===
Depending on market and manufacturing arrangements, the same basic machine can also appear under other names or build locations:
* '''Restysuma 20''' is documented as a name used for machines produced/sold by '''Hispano Olivetti'''.<ref name="rechnerlexikon-variants"/><ref name="calcinst-restysuma">{{cite web
 |title=Sumadoras (Adders) - Hispano Olivetti Restysuma 20 / Summa Prima 20 examples (Spain)
 |url=https://www.calculatinginstruments.com/3-sumadoras-adders/
 |website=CalculatingInstruments.com
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref>
* Some Prima 20 machines found in Australia are documented as coming from Olivetti factories in '''Argentina''' and from assemblers in '''South Africa'''.<ref name="johnwolff-origin">{{cite web
 |title=Olivetti Mechanical Calculators (Prima 20 origins: Italy, Argentina, assembled in South Africa)
 |url=https://www.johnwolff.id.au/calculators/Olivetti/Olivetti.htm
 |website=John Wolff's Web Museum
 |access-date=24 January 2026
}}</ref>
